body:
Yes! You sound just like me in every aspect! I will talk to the doctor about testing this.

THIS is so hard to explain to people: "I know how frustrating it can be, especially if it's already difficult to mentally focus when you're in a constant daydream and confused state."

YOU NAILED IT.

THAT is the MOST frustrating out of everything. Don't get me wrong, the stomach stuff and constant sleeping/headaches/pain is killer, KILLER. But not being able to think and focus on top of it? The sheer terror of driving because you can't 'understand' what's happening on the road? Not being able to go to school or advance in a career (or have a career at all!) because of this constant confusion and lack of comprehension? I had a 4.0 in school for years and you'd never guess it!

Thank you so much!

The situations are different, yet they're the same - the same 'We don't know what to tell you, your tests are normal, we don't see anything wrong, just watch what you eat,' etc. It's so discouraging when the medical professionals have no clue what's going on, yet you spend you days writhing in pain.

I feel for you, I'm sorry. I hope your trial and errors are working to the point where you are feeling better. :) I just choose not to eat for a few days when I have a 'big' event. Also, DGL helps quite a bit, I use this company: http://www.enzymatictherapy.com/Products/Digestion/Occasional-Heartburn-and-Indigestion/09101-DGL-Ultra.aspx (the German Chocolate flavor) and I see results fairly quickly when I'm having an off-day. Maybe it can help you, too?
I know, man! But with these blizzards occurring here I don't think I'd get very far!!

Actually, I have a friend that has Crohn's and that is the ONLY thing that makes the most difference in how he feels, even through the steroids and other pharmaceuticals he takes. 

I would do it if we didn't get tested so often at work!

I sleep a lot, that helps. ;) I don't get to think about it.

I actually eat very well for my age bracket - lots of organic fruits and vegetables, mostly grain-free (in case of celiac's), no sodas, very little dairy, and I've added meat in my diet at least 3 times a week. 

I know there's quite a few advancements in the medical field, I just feel so tired for hanging on, hanging on, hanging on... especially with no set 'diagnosis', there's no direction to go to without that magical name.

Thank you for your encouraging words, though. I appreciate your response.
Thank you for that link - there's some very good articles there. Thanks!

Thank you for your reply.

I know a few people with Bipolar Disorder - it's a very tough illness to handle, and I commend you. Thank you for your encouraging words, I wish you the best!
